title: Agentic Behavior Observatory
summary: A browser and command-line tool that scores GitHub repositories on six axes of agentic-behavior modeling, with file-and-line evidence, for researchers reviewing synthetic-population work.

narrative.problem: When someone builds a system that generates or evaluates synthetic populations at scale, it is hard to see what they are actually modeling and what they leave out: which demographic dimensions appear, which model versions the results rest on, and whether one agent's private context is kept from another's.
narrative.decision: Scores every repository by signal coverage against one taxonomy file (analyzer/signals.py) that is exported to the browser, so the dashboard and the CLI score identically and each point links to the file and line where its signal fired.
narrative.tradeoff: Regular expressions match vocabulary, not meaning: a repository that discusses a technique without implementing it still fires the signal, and a score measures coverage of the taxonomy rather than scientific quality.
narrative.limitation: Up to 120 files per repository are read, so large repositories are sampled rather than read whole, and the demographic vocabulary is a fixed English list that under-reports populations described in other terms.
narrative.caveat: Scores are signal coverage against the taxonomy, not a quality judgment; a low context-isolation score marks a boundary nobody wrote down, not proof of a leak.
